lines.t: I walked into the doggy parlor today,
Hair dryers hummin, pups at play.
Poor Joe sighed as he brushed his pup's chair,
Said, “Buddy’s gone, but love’s still there.”
I felt the hush, then peace like rain—
A lady said, “Hon, he’ll run again.”
No ear has heard, no heart could see,
What waits beyond for you and me.
He’s not gone, he’s just gone ahead,
Where tears are gone and love is spread.
For every howl, there’s joy reborn,
At the gates of light, on that golden morn.
Yahushua’s love is an overflowing fountain deep,
Restoring all, even those who sleep.
The clippers hum, soft fur takes flight,
But heaven feels a little closer tonight.
Joe smiles and says, “I’ll see him soon.”
Yes, she replied, all will be restored in the Kingdom, where nothing loses their bloom.
Before you call, He will reply,
While you are speaking, He draws nigh.
Ask, and hearts will surely mend—
For even this loss has no true end.
He’s not gone, he’s just gone ahead,
Where tears are gone and love is spread.
For every howl, there’s joy reborn,
At the gates of light, on that golden morn.
Yahushua’s love is an overflowing fountain deep,
Restoring all, even those who sleep.
So wash the coats and trim the bangs,
In every pup, a praise still hangs.
For just as He restores the years,
He gathers pets and wipes our tears.
No eye has seen such fields of grace,
Where furry friends will lick His face.
All things made new, hearts whole at last—
We’ll chase the dawn, forget the past.
Yahushua’s love is an endless, joyful spark,
He hears the woof before the bark!
At the doggy parlor, hope remains,
Through brushes, baths, and gentle chains.
For every pet we’ve loved and cried—
Will run again, right by our side.
